faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subheading: Everything you need to know about WhyNot.
faq.items.howItWorks.question: How does WhyNot find bugs automatically?
faq.items.howItWorks.answer: WhyNot deploys autonomous AI agents that navigate your web application like real users. They click buttons, fill forms, explore navigation paths, and monitor for console errors, broken layouts, failed API calls, and visual regressions — all without you writing a single line of test code.
faq.items.integration.question: How do I integrate WhyNot with my app?
faq.items.integration.answer: Just provide your app's URL. WhyNot works with any web application regardless of the tech stack — React, Vue, Angular, Next.js, Django, Rails, Laravel, WordPress, or any other framework. No SDK or code changes required.
faq.items.pricing.question: Is there a free tier?
faq.items.pricing.answer: Yes! Our free tier includes 50 test runs per month, up to 3 projects, and full access to AI bug detection and Playwright code generation. No credit card required to get started.
faq.items.security.question: Is my application data secure?
faq.items.security.answer: Absolutely. WhyNot runs tests in isolated browser sandboxes. We never store your application data, credentials, or user information. All connections are encrypted with TLS, and we are SOC 2 compliant.
faq.items.accuracy.question: How accurate is the bug detection?
faq.items.accuracy.answer: Our AI achieves a 99.2% accuracy rate with very low false positives. Each reported bug includes screenshots, console logs, network traces, and generated Playwright code so you can verify and reproduce it instantly.

landing.recon.sampleReport.title: Sample finding: reflected input escape bypass
landing.recon.sampleReport.description: A redacted excerpt from a real Recon report. Every finding includes an exact, reproducible proof-of-concept.
landing.recon.sampleReport.findingTitle: Reflected input escape bypass — High severity
landing.recon.sampleReport.findingBody: Input on the search endpoint is HTML-escaped but not attribute-escaped. An attacker can break out of a quoted attribute to inject event handlers.
landing.recon.sampleReport.findingSnippe:
GET /search?q=%22+onmouseover%3D[REDACTED]
Host: [REDACTED]

# Observed response reflects the payload
# inside a quoted HTML attribute without escaping.
